steps.title: Seat height
steps.text: Unload the arms, release the seat adjustment, and set the handles approximately across mid-chest. Let the lock engage fully.

steps.title: Starting reach
steps.text: If a start-position control is provided, choose a reach you can hold without the shoulders being pulled far behind you.

steps.title: Body support
steps.text: Sit with your back supported and feet stable; keep wrists aligned with the handles. Test the path before a working set.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: With the stack resting, insert the correct selector pin fully into one plate. Begin with a light test set.

steps.title: Seat and thigh pad
steps.text: Sit with both feet grounded. Adjust the thigh restraint until it holds the thighs comfortably without crushing them.

steps.title: Overhead attachment
steps.text: Check the bar and attachment clip. Choose a grip that allows the bar to travel in front of your head.

steps.title: Reach and clearance
steps.text: Use the intended steps or ask for help if the attachment is out of reach. Do not climb the frame or jump while holding a heavy stack.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Select a light load with the stack fully down; verify that the thigh restraint keeps you seated.

steps.title: Seat distance
steps.text: Adjust the seat or backrest so your feet reach the platform and the pelvis stays against the support throughout your chosen depth.

steps.title: Foot placement
steps.text: Place the whole foot on the platform, approximately hip-to-shoulder width as comfortable. Keep knees tracking with the toes.

steps.title: Stop and return
steps.text: Identify the re-rack or stop mechanism on your model. Test it lightly; do not force deep knee bend or snap the knees backward.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Use the selector only with the stack resting. A plate-loaded sled has different catches: follow its placard and get an orientation before use.

eq_smith.name: Smith Machine

steps.title: Bar hooks
steps.text: Practice the rotation that releases and re-engages the hooks using an unloaded or minimally loaded bar. Confirm both sides catch.

steps.title: Safety stops
steps.text: Place the two stops equally, just below your intended bottom position, so a failed rep cannot trap you. Test before adding plates.

steps.title: Bench or stance
steps.text: Center a stable bench or your stance under the actual rail path. Inclined rails may require a different position from vertical rails.

steps.title: Load and clearance
steps.text: Load both sides evenly and use the model's required collars. Clear the path and re-hook securely before stepping away.

eq_smith.caution: Smith bars have different starting resistance and rail angles. A hook is not a substitute for correctly set safety stops.

steps.title: Choose the pair
steps.text: Check the weight markings and handle condition. For two-handed work, use a matched pair unless your exercise intentionally calls for a single weight.

steps.title: Adjustable locks
steps.text: For adjustable dumbbells, follow the maker's selector or collar procedure and verify every plate is locked before lifting; fixed dumbbells have no adjustment.

steps.title: Pickup and start
steps.text: Clear space, use a controlled hip and knee bend to collect the weights, and use the exercise's intended start position.

steps.title: Support and return
steps.text: If a bench is needed, lock it first. Choose a load you can return safely; keep fingers clear when re-racking.

eq_adjustable_bench.name: Adjustable Bench

steps.title: Back-pad angle
steps.text: Support the pad with no one on the bench. Release the intended pin or ladder and choose flat, incline or upright as the exercise requires.

steps.title: Locking mechanism
steps.text: Let the pin fully seat or the support bar fully enter the ladder notch. Gently test the pad before adding bodyweight or dumbbells.

steps.title: Seat position
steps.text: Adjust and lock the seat if the model allows it, so you are supported without sliding. Keep fingers away from hinges.

steps.title: Floor and clearance
steps.text: Set the bench on a stable, level surface with all feet contacting the floor. Respect its combined user-and-load limit.

eq_adjustable_bench.caution: The back-pad angle is exercise-specific; no single notch fits every movement. An adjustable bench is not automatically rated as a step-up platform.

eq_x_cable.name: Cable Station

steps.title: Pulley height
steps.text: With the stack resting and cable unloaded, support the carriage, release its adjustment, slide to the required height, then check the lock has engaged.

steps.title: Attachment clip
steps.text: Use an attachment rated for the station. Close its clip fully and check that the cable end, handle or ankle cuff is secure.

steps.title: Weight selector
steps.text: Insert the station's selector pin fully with the stack down. For two-arm exercises, check each stack independently; pulley ratios can differ.

steps.title: Line of pull
steps.text: Position your body so the cable runs freely and does not rub against you, the frame or another cable. Test the full range with a light load.

eq_x_cable.caution: High pulley: pushdowns and pulldowns. Low pulley: many curls and pull-throughs. Chest height: many Pallof presses. The exact exercise setup takes priority.

steps.title: J-hook height
steps.text: Set both hooks to the same height so the bar can be unracked without a tiptoe reach or deep squat. Check each hook is fully secured.

steps.title: Safety arms
steps.text: Set both safeties equally for your squat or bench range; test with a light bar that they catch it without trapping your body.

steps.title: Plates and collars
steps.text: Load compatible plates evenly on both sides and secure the required collars. Use the rack and bar within their rated capacity.

steps.title: Bench and exit
steps.text: For bench pressing, center and lock a suitable bench; arrange appropriate spotting. Rehearse the unrack and re-rack before working sets.

steps.title: Grip bends
steps.text: Choose matching angled grip positions that keep the wrists comfortable. Center the hands equally around the middle of the bar.

steps.title: Sleeves and collars
steps.text: Identify whether the bar is fixed-weight or plate-loaded. For plate-loaded bars, fit compatible plates and secure collars on both ends.

steps.title: Starting support
steps.text: Use a stable rack, bench or controlled floor pickup appropriate to the exercise. Keep the area around the bar clear.

steps.title: Light rehearsal
steps.text: Practice the curl or extension path and a safe return before using a working load; do not carry a loaded bar over someone's head.

steps.title: Handle choice
steps.text: Select the intended high or low handles, if the bar offers both, before loading. Different handle heights change the starting range.

steps.title: Even loading
steps.text: Load both sleeves equally, fit compatible collars and check that the plates and handles are secure.

steps.title: Stance
steps.text: Stand centered inside the frame with hands evenly placed. Keep feet and shins clear of the frame as you hinge down.

steps.title: Clear landing
steps.text: Lift and set down in a clear, level area. Return the bar evenly without trapping the toes beneath the plates or frame.

steps.title: Hip-pad height
steps.text: Adjust the pad so its upper edge supports the upper thighs just below the hip crease, allowing the hips to hinge freely.

steps.title: Foot restraints
steps.text: Place feet on the platform and fit the ankle or calf restraints as shown on the placard. Check they hold without painful pressure.

steps.title: Range
steps.text: Start with bodyweight. Hinge to a comfortable depth and return to a straight, controlled body line without throwing the back upward.

steps.title: Entry and exit
steps.text: Use the machine's handles to mount and leave the bench. Confirm the pad adjustment is locked before leaning forward.

steps.title: Seat and pivot
steps.text: Adjust the seat to the machine's torso-alignment markers; sit with pelvis and feet supported.

steps.title: Upper-body pad
steps.text: Fit the chest, shoulder or arm pad as your model directs. Do not press a pad against your neck.

steps.title: Start range
steps.text: Select a start position you can reach without being forced into a large back arch. Practice the curl without momentum.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Choose light resistance with the stack resting; use trunk control instead of pulling hard with the arms.

steps.title: Assistance
steps.text: On counterweighted machines, more selected weight usually means more assistance. Check the placard; this is different from a normal resistance stack.

steps.title: Handles and platform
steps.text: Set adjustable handle width if provided. Locate the steps and moving knee or foot platform before mounting.

steps.title: Controlled mounting
steps.text: Hold the handles, step onto the intended supports and transfer weight to the assistance platform gradually. Keep clear of its travel.

steps.title: Controlled dismount
steps.text: Let the platform return under control, using the intended steps. Do not jump off or change the selector while it is moving.

steps.title: Assistance
steps.text: Check the placard: a heavier selection usually provides more assistance on a counterweight machine. Start with enough help to control the full rep.

steps.title: Overhead grip
steps.text: Choose reachable handles and a comfortable grip. Use the intended steps rather than climbing the frame.

steps.title: Knee or foot support
steps.text: Mount as shown, holding the handles while you transfer weight onto the moving support. Keep fingers clear of its mechanism.

steps.title: Dismount
steps.text: Return the platform slowly and step onto the designated steps before releasing the handles. Keep the selector unchanged while moving.

steps.title: Back and shoulder pads
steps.text: Fit under the shoulder pads with your back supported; adjust the pad or start height if your model allows it.

steps.title: Foot platform
steps.text: Place feet securely on the platform in a comfortable stance; rehearse a depth that keeps heels and pelvis supported.

steps.title: Safety catches
steps.text: Locate the release handles and set any adjustable stops before loading. Practice releasing and re-racking with minimal resistance.

steps.title: Even loading
steps.text: Add plates evenly and use the specified retention system. Never move a safety stop with the carriage loaded on it.

steps.title: Seat and backrest
steps.text: Sit with your pelvis and back supported; adjust the seat if available and place feet on the intended supports.

steps.title: Pad orientation
steps.text: For abduction, the pads resist the outside of the knees or thighs as you move outward. Follow the model's conversion instructions if shared with adduction.

steps.title: Starting width
steps.text: Use the unloaded range lever to choose a comfortable, narrower starting position. Release it only once the setting is engaged.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Select light resistance, use the handles for stability and keep the pelvis still as the legs move apart.

steps.title: Seat and backrest
steps.text: Adjust for a supported torso and stable feet, using the machine's designated footrests.

steps.title: Pad orientation
steps.text: For adduction, pads contact the inside of the knees or thighs as you bring the legs together. Verify any dual-function conversion is locked.

steps.title: Starting width
steps.text: Choose a comfortable starting opening with the unloaded range lever; do not force a wide groin stretch.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Use a light stack selection and bring the pads inward slowly without bouncing or letting the stack crash.

steps.title: Seat height
steps.text: Adjust the unloaded seat so the handles meet the upper-chest pressing line without forcing the elbows far behind you.

steps.title: Starting handles
steps.text: Set a comfortable start position if the model offers one, and check the entry or start-assist lever.

steps.title: Back and feet
steps.text: Keep the back against the inclined support and the feet stable; test that the handle path clears your shoulders comfortably.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Select a light stack setting, or load plate horns evenly as the placard requires. Keep clear of moving lever arms.

steps.title: Seat height
steps.text: Adjust the seat so your shoulders align with the machine's indicated movement axis.

steps.title: Arm pads
steps.text: Fit the pads against the intended part of the upper arms near the elbows, not against the neck or wrists.

steps.title: Range and posture
steps.text: Sit supported and test a comfortable side-raise range without shrugging; adjust a start stop if provided.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Choose a small load and raise both arms smoothly without driving against the pads with the trunk.

steps.title: Back-pad position
steps.text: Move the back pad so the thighs rest on the seat and the knee joint lines up with the machine pivot.

steps.title: Knee alignment
steps.text: Check the side of the knee against the pivot marker. Do not use the kneecap as a pad or pressure point.

steps.title: Shin roller and start
steps.text: Fit the roller across the lower shin above the ankle, clear of the foot. Set a comfortable knee-bend starting position.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Select a light load and test smooth knee extension without kicking, lifting the hips or snapping backward.

steps.title: Seat and pelvic restraint
steps.text: Adjust the seat and any lap or thigh restraint so the pelvis is held as the placard specifies.

steps.title: Back pad
steps.text: Fit the moving pad against the intended upper-back region, never directly against the neck.

steps.title: Start angle
steps.text: Choose a small, comfortable starting range; do not force spinal movement to reach a preset endpoint.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Begin with a light selection and controlled movement. Get individualized guidance if spinal loading is restricted for you.

steps.title: Knee position
steps.text: Lie on the bench so the knee joint lines up with the machine pivot and the thighs are supported.

steps.title: Ankle roller
steps.text: Adjust the roller onto the lower calf just above the heel, avoiding direct pressure on the Achilles tendon.

steps.title: Hip support
steps.text: Keep the pelvis on the pad and select a comfortable start range. Hold the intended handles without pulling the back into a large arch.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Select a light load and test a smooth curl before loading further; keep clear of the moving leg lever.

steps.title: Seat height
steps.text: Set the seat so handles or forearm pads align with the intended chest-fly path, approximately across chest level.

steps.title: Arm start position
steps.text: Adjust the unloaded arms so you can reach them without being pulled into an extreme shoulder stretch.

steps.title: Chest or reverse mode
steps.text: If the machine converts to reverse fly, follow its conversion instructions and face the correct support pad for that mode.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Start with a light selection and keep the torso supported throughout the opening and closing path.

steps.title: Seat height
steps.text: Adjust the seat so the upper arms rest comfortably on the pad without shrugging the shoulders.

steps.title: Elbow pivot
steps.text: Align the elbows with the machine's indicated rotation axis. The pad supports the upper arms, not a painfully compressed elbow point.

steps.title: Grip and range
steps.text: Choose a wrist-friendly grip and a start position that does not force the elbows into full extension.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Start light and test a slow curl and return while the upper arms remain supported.

steps.title: Seat and feet
steps.text: Place the balls of the feet securely on the step, with room for a small controlled heel drop.

steps.title: Thigh restraint
steps.text: Fit the pad just above the knees, snug enough to transfer the load without pressing painfully on the kneecaps.

steps.title: Release and re-rack
steps.text: With a light load, raise enough to disengage the latch as the placard directs. Practice re-engaging it before the set.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Load both sides evenly if plate-loaded, or set the stack pin fully. Do not bounce the heels at the bottom.

steps.title: Backrest
steps.text: Adjust the back support until the knee joints align with the machine pivot and the thighs are supported.

steps.title: Thigh restraint
steps.text: Fit the upper restraint above the knees to hold the thighs gently against the seat; do not clamp the kneecaps.

steps.title: Lower-leg roller
steps.text: Place the lower roller on the lower calf above the heel. Choose a start angle you can reach comfortably.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Select light resistance and check that the pelvis stays supported during both curl and return.

steps.title: Seat and chest pad
steps.text: Adjust the seat and any chest support so you can reach the handles without rounding or lifting off the pad.

steps.title: Handle path
steps.text: Choose a grip that allows a comfortable elbow path toward the ribs; keep wrists aligned with the handles.

steps.title: Foot support
steps.text: Place the feet on the intended braces and keep the torso steady. A chest-supported model reduces the need to hold the torso upright.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Use light resistance to test the entire reach and pull before adding load; keep hands clear of lever hinges.

steps.title: Seat height
steps.text: Set the unloaded seat so the start handles are around shoulder level and you can grip them without forcing the shoulders backward.

steps.title: Grip
steps.text: Choose the provided neutral or overhand handles that allow comfortable wrist and elbow alignment.

steps.title: Back support
steps.text: Keep the trunk against the pad and feet stable. Test the overhead path without a large lower-back arch.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Select a light stack setting or load both plate horns evenly. Confirm a controlled return before a working set.

steps.title: Shoulder-pad height
steps.text: Adjust the unloaded pad or start position so you can enter and stand tall without ducking under a heavily loaded pad.

steps.title: Forefoot placement
steps.text: Keep the balls of both feet securely on the platform; leave only a comfortable amount of heel overhang.

steps.title: Latch and support
steps.text: Identify the release and re-rack control, use the intended handles, and practice with a light load.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Fit the selector fully or load plate horns evenly. Keep the knees controlled rather than bouncing them with each rep.

steps.title: Seat and lower-body pads
steps.text: Fit the seat and leg or thigh pads so the lower body is supported as the model intends.

steps.title: Upper-body handles
steps.text: Hold the provided handles without twisting the neck or pulling the shoulders into an awkward position.

steps.title: Starting angle
steps.text: Choose a modest rotation range using the unloaded range control. Do not force the trunk to the machine's maximum stop.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.text: Start light and rotate slowly; reverse direction using the model's instructions rather than twisting against a fixed restraint.

steps.title: Seat height
steps.text: Set the seat so upper arms rest on the intended pad without the shoulders rising.

steps.title: Elbow axis
steps.text: Align the elbow joints with the machine's pivot markers and keep pressure on the upper-arm pad, not the elbow tips.

steps.title: Handles and range
steps.text: Grip with wrists aligned and select a comfortable start angle without forcing the elbows into a deep bend.

steps.title: Resistance
